plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single sketch on an unlabeled coordinate plane showing a position vector broken into its horizontal and vertical parts. Two thin axes with arrowheads at all four ends meet at the origin; neither axis carries a name or numbers, though a few short tick marks are spaced along them. An orange arrow runs from the origin up and to the right into the first quadrant and is labeled v = ai + bj, with v, i, and j set in bold. A dark blue arrow extends from the origin along the horizontal axis to the point lying directly beneath the orange arrow's tip and is labeled ai below the axis. A second dark blue arrow rises vertically from that point to the tip of the orange arrow and is labeled bj. The two blue arrows and the orange one enclose a right triangle whose legs are the components and whose hypotenuse is the vector. Drawing the components as arrows joined head to tail makes the vector read as their sum rather than as an abstract pair. The sketch supports the magnitude of v being sqrt(a^2 + b^2), read straight off the legs of the triangle.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Because a vector's orthogonal components form the legs of a right triangle, vector addition inherently connects algebraic components to geometric lengths via the Pythagorean theorem.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Axes are thin, black, unnumbered lines with simple tick marks. The orange vector is thicker than the axes. The dark blue component vectors form a path along the x-axis then parallel to the y-axis. In 'Vector Components' mode, use bold mathematical styling for vectors (v, i, j) and italics for scalars (a, b). In 'Magnitude Triangle' mode, the blue lines can lose their arrowheads (or keep them but change labels to simple italic 'a' and 'b') and a small right-angle square should appear where the horizontal and vertical segments meet. Ensure labels move dynamically as the sliders change a and b.

discrepancies: The text labels for the vectors are severely truncated (displaying only 'i' or 'j'), completely missing their values or variables due to a text-rendering bug.
The original figure uses generic symbolic labels (ai, bj, v = ai + bj), whereas the generated figure substitutes numerical values based on the slider state.
The arrowheads of the vertical blue vector and the resultant orange vector overlap awkwardly at their shared terminal point, rather than meeting cleanly.
evaluation.notes: The interactive geometry correctly builds upon the source with sliders and a magnitude mode, but a rendering bug in how tspans are appended truncates all vector labels to a single character ('i' or 'j'), losing the core mathematical expressions.
action_items: Fix `formatText` to properly render multi-segment text in SVG.js v3: instead of calling `el.tspan()` repeatedly (which is causing segments to be overwritten or omitted), use `el.text(add => { segments.forEach(s => ... ) })` or construct a single combined text string.
Consider displaying the original symbolic formulas (e.g. v = ai + bj) prominently alongside the numerical version to maintain the textbook's level of abstraction.
Slightly inset the endpoints of the blue vertical vector and the orange resultant vector so their arrowheads don't visually clip through each other at the terminal vertex.
